clue.text: Top of plant under-developed, cut back

indicators.note: the top of a word in a clue is its first letter, here of plant
the word under is developed into a new form, its letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: A gardener's note: the stunted tip of a plant was trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes 'under-developed' look like one adjective for a stunted plant, but 'under' is the anagram material and 'developed' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune a shrub is to trim its growth, so a pruned plant has been trimmed.

clue.text: Errors in wage packets

parts.note: read as mistakes made over pay, the clue describes the paper slips found in pay envelopes

explanation.walkthrough: Slips are errors and wages are pay, so a pay slip reads as a pay error; really it is the itemised statement tucked into a wage packet.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the printed statements of earnings handed to employees with their wages.

clue.text: Woeful sound shows Lulu's up and getting into a bother

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lulu is a girl's name and a Scottish pop singer, taken as written

indicators.note: the words into a are put in a bother, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: The pop singer Lulu is heard wailing as she climbs into a fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LULU into ULUL; 'bother' scrambles INTO A into ATION; 'getting' just joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A wailing howl of grief is a mournful cry, exactly a woeful sound.

clue.text: Male chorus provides an encore

indicators.note: the phrase male chorus supplies the answer from inside its letters, across the word break

explanation.surface: A men's choir obliges the audience with one more number.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat of a sound or performance is a repetition, which an encore is.

clue.text: Buy tea in a bag

indicators.note: the word for tea is placed in the middle of the word for a bag

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy a teabag.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something by paying for it is to make a purchase, as a verb.

clue.text: R Mugabe gives offence

indicators.note: the letters of R Mugabe give way and yield a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The Zimbabwean leader Robert Mugabe causes diplomatic offence.
explanation.walkthrough: R Mugabe is the former president of Zimbabwe; his initial and surname rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so the word means a sense of injury or resentment.

clue.text: Accomplished boxers will be upset if they have to be

definitions.meaning: achieved or performed, as a task done to completion

definitions.text: boxers will be upset if they have to be
definitions.meaning: a knocked-out boxer is lifted and taken from the ring, which no boxer wants

explanation.surface: A dry remark about fighters' pride at being stretchered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accomplished' looks like praise for skilled boxers but is a definition of its own; the rest says what happens to a beaten fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that has been executed has been performed fully; a felled boxer is literally borne from the ring.

clue.text: Jason's craft heads north in the atmosphere

indicators.note: the ship heads, or goes in front of, the letter for north

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: The Argonauts' ship sails northwards through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble gas making up nearly one per cent of air is a component found in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Last though almost sure to hold out

definitions.meaning: to last is to continue or persist over time
to hold out is to bear up and not give in

explanation.surface: Something holds firm though it nearly fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though almost sure to' links the two senses, both meaning carry on and survive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean persist: to continue in time, and to withstand hardship without yielding.

clue.text: Gaoled after a disturbance, in which one should know better!

definitions.text: in which one should know better!

indicators.note: the word gaoled is disturbed, its letters shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook jailed after a riot, at an age when they ought to know better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaoled' is the British spelling of jailed. The exclamation mark flags the joke: the elderly are expected to have learned sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The later years of life are the stage when long experience should bring wisdom.

clue.text: Where old friends aren't expected to meet

definitions.text: Where old friends aren't expected to meet

parts.words: Where old friends aren't expected to meet
parts.note: old seems to mean long-standing, but it means aged: this meeting place is for the young

explanation.walkthrough: 'old friends' suggests a reunion; read 'old' literally, as elderly, and the place is a club for teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre for teenagers' leisure activities is no place for elderly members.

clue.text: 50% of dirigibles are of this construction

definitions.text: 50% of dirigibles are of this construction

parts.words: 50% of dirigibles are of this construction
parts.note: airships come in two kinds, with or without an internal frame, and the clue names the framed kind

explanation.walkthrough: The first half of 'dirigibles', DIRIG, also rearranges into the answer, a bonus hint inside the cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Airships with a stiff metal framework, like the Zeppelins, are stiff-framed rather than blimps.

clue.text: An electric wire to act as a conductor

definitions.meaning: a flex or cable joining an appliance to a power supply
to direct an orchestra or guide others, to go in front

explanation.definitionFit: A cable connecting a device is a flex; to guide or direct a band is to head it.

clue.text: Holidaymaker Veronica at play

indicators.note: the letters of Veronica at are put into play, rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A woman named Veronica relaxing on her holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking time off on a trip is a tourist, the American term for a holidaymaker.

clue.text: Poorly valued live entertainment

indicators.note: valued live is put together badly, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Live entertainment that critics rate low.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety theatre of songs, comedy and acts is a form of stage entertainment.

clue.text: Secret service man on lowest rate of pay

definitions.meaning: confidential, not for public knowledge

definitions.text: service man on lowest rate of pay
definitions.meaning: the lowest rank of soldier in the army, paid least

explanation.surface: A secret agent who is badly paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Confidential matters are personal; the most junior army rank is the least-paid soldier.

clue.text: At last I have something for a salad

parts.note: at last means in the end, giving the word end

explanation.surface: A diner relieved finally to have some salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicory-like leaves with a bitter taste are a common salad vegetable.

clue.text: Brilliant featherweight

definitions.meaning: a bright flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor Very
weighing almost nothing, extremely low in weight

explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is a brilliant signal flare; anything weighing almost nothing is extremely low in weight.

clue.text: Lent is brought forward

definitions.meaning: lent as money, given on loan
moved earlier or pushed onwards

explanation.surface: The Christian fast falls earlier this year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' looks like the season before Easter, but it is the past tense of lend: money advanced is lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Money advanced is money loaned; a date advanced has been moved earlier.

clue.text: Very nervous near the brink

definitions.meaning: tense and jumpy, with nerves frayed
close to the edge of a drop

explanation.definitionFit: Being jittery is like teetering at the rim of a cliff, both literally and figuratively.

clue.text: Understanding French

definitions.meaning: an agreement between nations
the word is borrowed straight from French

explanation.definitionFit: An informal pact between states is an agreement, and the word itself comes from French.

clue.text: Evened the score by bribery?

definitions.meaning: settled a debt or levelled a contest
to square an official is to bribe them

explanation.surface: A match result levelled by paying off the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: To even accounts is to settle up; paying someone off is slang for squaring them.

clue.text: Works up to employ a partner

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work, so works gives ops
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A firm takes on extra staff to hire a business partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OPS (works, from opus) into SPO; 'to employ' then gives USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband or wife is one's marriage partner.

clue.text: Tablet providing uplift and stimulus

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up both words reads them from bottom to top

parts.note: a pill is a tablet of medicine
providing means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: A pill that gives a mood boost and a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplift' turns the whole run PILL + IF upwards, reading it backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost or encouragement is a spur or stimulus.

clue.text: Hostelry getting acclaim for modernisation

explanation.surface: A pub praised for its refit.
explanation.definitionFit: Introducing new methods or ideas is updating, which is what modernisation means.

clue.text: Hurry indoors to reduce waist of garment

definitions.meaning: to pop quickly into a place
to take in a dress or trousers at the waist

explanation.definitionFit: Popping briefly into a shop is dashing in; a tailor taking in a waistband narrows it.

clue.text: Leaf-destroying parasite

indicators.note: the word leaf is destroyed, broken up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A pest that wrecks foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaf-destroying' suggests a leaf-eating bug, but the hyphen hides an anagram of LEAF. The printed answer PLEA is a typo: the clue builds FLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A small jumping insect feeding on blood of mammals is a classic parasite.

clue.text: It tastes sweet, but schoolboys don't like it

definitions.meaning: sugar is made from a tall sweet grass
a stick once used to beat pupils as punishment

explanation.definitionFit: Sugar comes from a sweet grass stalk; a rod for corporal punishment was dreaded by pupils.

clue.text: Turnover in coats

parts.note: turnover suggests business sales, but means the folded-back flap at the front of a jacket

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' reads like a trade figure for coat sales; it is literally the part of the front that turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: The folded flap on each side of a jacket front below the collar is turned over.

clue.text: Upset at closing, remembering happier times?

indicators.note: the words at closing are upset, knocked over into a new letter order

explanation.surface: A regular saddened at a pub's closure, recalling the good old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful longing for the past is sentimental yearning for happier days.

clue.text: Aid to look-out on the bridge

definitions.text: Aid to look-out on the bridge

parts.words: Aid to look-out on the bridge
parts.note: bridge suggests a ship's lookout, but means the bridge of the nose, where these glasses clip

explanation.walkthrough: A ship's bridge and lookout are the false picture; these spectacles grip the bridge of the nose with no arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip-on spectacles held by a spring on the nose aid one's eyesight.

clue.text: Hot tea he'd spilt

indicators.note: tea he'd is spilt, its letters scattered and regathered in another order

explanation.surface: A man spills his scalding tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Something warmed up is hot; also hot-tempered, as in a fierce argument.
